subject.title: [Bug]: opencode-go/minimax-m3 thinking content leaks to channel via Anthropic Messages path

question: Should maintainers require live opencode-go/minimax-m3 proof before authorizing a new security-sensitive fix, and should the fix force disabled thinking or use a proxy-specific sanitizer if disabled thinking suppresses final output?
rationale: Current source proves the missing provider wrapper branch, but MiniMax M3 disabled-thinking behavior can affect final delivery, so choosing the safe mitigation requires maintainer/security intent plus live provider evidence.

options.title: Require live proof before the fix
options.body: Capture redacted opencode-go/minimax-m3 terminal, log, or Telegram proof first, then land the provider-local disable-or-sanitize fix that preserves final text.

options.title: Fold into the broader reasoning-leak umbrella
options.body: Treat this as a slice of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89473 only if maintainers want one shared reasoning-leak project to own provider-proxy and channel leak variants together.

options.title: Accept forced disabled thinking now
options.body: Proceed directly with a disabled-thinking payload override, accepting the risk that final answer delivery may fail for this proxy until live proof catches it.

recommendation.title: Require live proof before the fix
recommendation.body: Capture redacted opencode-go/minimax-m3 terminal, log, or Telegram proof first, then land the provider-local disable-or-sanitize fix that preserves final text.

likelyOwner.reason: This account authored the most relevant merged opencode-go reasoning sanitizer and touched the exact stream wrapper boundary.
